reserveReview.rationale: Curated rows mirror the live Circle transparency adapter's two EURC slice identities, with weights from the Aug 06, 2026 weekly disclosure (EUR 391.19M other bank deposits, EUR 5.71M deposits at systemically important institutions). These rows are the classification scaffold for the live adapter; the Deloitte June 30, 2026 examination (EUR 384.7M all-cash reserves vs EUR 382.0M EURC, read directly this pass) is recorded on the proofOfReserves latestReport and corroborates the all-deposit composition. compositionAsOf is intentionally absent: the weekly disclosure is a rolling live basis, not the examined balance-sheet date.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Circle's ACPR-filed MiCA white paper (section D.3) states that funds received in exchange for EURC are protected against any recourse by other creditors of Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS, including in enforcement or insolvency proceedings, and the EURC Terms and Deloitte's May 2026 examination define reserves as unencumbered segregated accounts apart from corporate funds, held on behalf of and for the benefit of holders. Bank identities, institution count, provider-level shares, custodian-replacement arrangements, and rehypothecation terms are not published; the May 2026 report shows the reserve is 100% cash at regulated financial institutions. Issuer pages describe the reserve banks as regulated financial institutions in the EEA, while one circle.com/eurc footnote states cash is held at US financial institutions; account-level placement is not public.
